title: Pair programming
shortDescription: Talk through a coding problem together, thinking out loud as you go.
communicativeGoals: Suggest an approach and justify it
React to a partner's reasoning and question trade-offs
grammarTargets: First conditional for proposing approaches ('If we do X, then...')
Modal verbs for suggestions ('We could...', 'We should...')
conversationMoves: Suggest an approach to a coding problem
React to their reasoning the way a real engineering partner would
Question trade-offs and suggest edge cases
warmUpPrompts: How would you start solving this kind of problem?
What's the first question you'd ask before writing any code?
rolePlayPrompts: Propose an approach to a problem and defend it when I push back.
Walk me through debugging a piece of code that isn't working.
challengePrompts: Explain why you'd choose one data structure over another.
Disagree with my suggested approach and propose a better one.
successCriteria: Learner explains their reasoning, not just the final answer
Learner considers at least one edge case unprompted
Learner responds constructively when their approach is questioned

suggestedReviewItems.content: edge case (noun) — an unusual input that could break the code
First conditional for proposing technical approaches

focusPlaceholder: e.g. a specific kind of problem (algorithms, debugging, design)
